knowledge:
- key_parameters: sig_transcripts=A vector of transcript IDs associated with degradation, typically obtained using select_transcripts() ;; cell_component=A logical parameter in select_transcripts() which, when TRUE, selects transcripts from a model that includes cell type proportions ;; top1000/top1500=Logical parameters in select_transcripts() to select the union of the top 1000 or 1500 degradation-associated transcripts ;; assayname=The name of the assay in the RangedSummarizedExperiment to use for calculations (e.g., "tpm") ;; mod=A model matrix containing biological and demographic covariates (e.g., Diagnosis, Age, Sex) used to estimate the number of required PCs ;; k=The number of quality surrogate variables (PCs) to retain, calculated using k_qsvs()
- alternatives: The 2016 qSVA framework used expressed regions (identified via derfinder), which are computationally expensive to identify and not standard pipeline outputs. The current qsvaR package uses transcript-level quantification (e.g., from Salmon), which is simpler and more standard. Alternatively, the SPEAQeasy pipeline can be run with the --qsva flag to generate the transcript RangedSummarizedExperiment directly.
- when_to_use: Use this package when performing differential expression or other downstream transcriptomic analyses on postmortem human brain tissue RNA-seq data to correct for sample degradation.
- pitfalls: Users must set a random seed using set.seed() before running k_qsvs() or qSVA() because they internally call sva::num.sv(), which requires a seed for reproducible results. Additionally, differential expression analysis must be performed on the full transcript dataset (rse_tx), not the subsetted degradation-associated transcripts (DegTx), as PCs are only meant to model the degradation, while DE requires the full dataset.

workflows.name: qsv_degradation_correction
workflows.intent: Identify and extract quality surrogate variables (qSVs) to correct for bench degradation in postmortem brain RNA-seq data, and perform degradation-corrected differential expression analysis.
input: rse_tx (RangedSummarizedExperiment containing transcript-level expression data, such as TPMs, and sample metadata in colData)
workflows.stages: 1. Filter the input RangedSummarizedExperiment for minimum expression and relevant samples ;; 2. Extract degradation-associated transcripts using getDegTx() and select_transcripts() ;; 3. Compute principal components of the degraded transcripts using getPCs() ;; 4. Define the experimental design matrix and calculate the optimal number of PCs (k) using k_qsvs() ;; 5. Extract the final qSV matrix using get_qsvs() (or perform steps 2-5 in one step using the wrapper function qSVA()) ;; 6. Perform differential expression analysis using limma by appending the qSVs to the design matrix ;; 7. Evaluate the correction quality by plotting t-statistics against degradation t-statistics using DEqual()
workflows.code:
# obtain transcripts with degradation signature
DegTx <- getDegTx(
  rse_tx, sig_transcripts = select_transcripts(cell_component = TRUE)
)
dim(DegTx)

pcTx <- getPCs(rse_tx = DegTx, assayname = "tpm")

# design a basic model matrix to model the number of pcs needed
mod <- model.matrix(~ Dx + Age + Sex + Race + Region,
    data = colData(rse_tx)
)

## To ensure that the results are reproducible, you will need to set a
## random seed with the set.seed() function. Internally, we are using
## sva::num.sv() which needs a random seed to ensure reproducibility of the
## results.
set.seed(20230621)

# use k qsvs function to return a integer of pcs needed
k <- k_qsvs(rse_tx = DegTx, mod = mod, assayname = "tpm")
print(k)

# get_qsvs use k to subset our pca analysis
qsvs <- get_qsvs(qsvPCs = pcTx, k = k)
dim(qsvs)

## To ensure that the results are reproducible, you will need to set a
## random seed with the set.seed() function. Internally, we are using
## sva::num.sv() which needs a random seed to ensure reproducibility of the
## results.
set.seed(20230621)

## Example use of the wrapper function qSVA()
qsvs_wrapper <- qSVA(
    rse_tx = rse_tx,
    sig_transcripts = select_transcripts(cell_component = TRUE),
    mod = mod, 
    assayname = "tpm"
)
dim(qsvs_wrapper)

# create a model.matrix with demographic info and qsvs
mod_qSVA <- cbind(mod, qsvs)

# log tranform transcript expression
txExprs <- log2(assays(rse_tx)$tpm + 1)

# linear model differential expression
fitTx <- lmFit(txExprs, mod_qSVA)

# generate empirical bayes for DE
eBTx <- eBayes(fitTx)

# get DE results table
sigTx <- topTable(eBTx,
    coef = 2,
    p.value = 1, number = nrow(rse_tx)
)
head(sigTx)

## Subset the topTable() results to keep just the t-statistic
DE_noqsv <- data.frame(t = sigTx_noqsv$t, row.names = rownames(sigTx_noqsv))
DE <- data.frame(t = sigTx$t, row.names = rownames(sigTx))

## Generate a DEqual() plot using the model results without qSVs
DEqual(DE_noqsv)

## Generate a DEqual() plot using the model results with qSVs
DEqual(DE)
